note: What each approved topic means, for judging whether a post is on target. Narrative-first: we look for claims and calls to action about policing in the UK, never for individuals. Lawful political opinion (for example criticism of the police or of 'two-tier policing') is NOT a hit on its own.

P01.label: Fake police notices and curfews
P01.hit: A UK post sharing, warning about or debunking a fake police notice, letter, leaflet or curfew.

P02.label: Spiking claims
P02.hit: A UK post claiming, warning about or questioning drink or needle spiking incidents and the police response.

P03.label: Fake fines and penalty scams
P03.hit: A UK post about scam texts, emails or letters pretending to be police or council fines or penalty notices.

P04.label: Suspect identity rumours after an attack
P04.hit: A UK post naming or speculating about the identity, nationality, religion or immigration status of a suspect after a violent incident, or claiming police are hiding it.

P05.label: Police cover-up claims
P05.hit: A UK post claiming the police are covering up, lying about or hiding the truth of a specific incident.

P06.label: Calls to gather at sites
P06.hit: A UK post calling people to turn up at an asylum hotel, mosque, police station or similar site, or to take to the streets. Also a hit (for the debunk variants P06b): a UK post or reply that debunks a false claim about policing, protests, asylum hotels or UK law, because it shows which false claim is circulating.

P07.label: Old footage passed off as new
P07.hit: A UK post sharing old or out-of-context footage of disorder as current, or pointing out that such footage is old.

P08.label: Fake official statements
P08.hit: A UK post about a fake, doctored or misattributed police or Home Office statement or screenshot.
